newsitem.title: MOROCCO: World Bank to open permanent mission in Morocco.
newsitem.headline: World Bank to open permanent mission in Morocco.

text.p: The World Bank, which is to launch a three-year assistance strategy plan to help Morocco speed up its economic reforms, plans to open a permanent mission in Morocco, a bank official said on Monday.

"To supervise closely its Moroccan assistance strategy plan for 1997-2000 period, the World Bank plans to open a permanent mission in Morocco," said the official, who is member of a delegation visiting the kingdom.
But he declined to give more details.
Officials said earlier the office is expected to be established in Morocco's financial centre of Casablanca where the bank's arm International Finance Corporation has already a branch.

In a recent report, the World Bank urged Morocco to speed up its economic and social reforms to ensure a sustainable annual growth of 5.0 to 6.0 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and reduce social disparities between urban and rural areas.
Morocco's economy posted a growth of 11.8 percent in 1996 and would register between 3.0 to 4.0 percent growth in 1997, Finance Ministry Mohamed Kabbaj has said.
Kabbaj also noted that national saving rose to 19 percent of GDP against 16 percent in 1995.
But investment dropped to 20.5 percent in 1996, from 22 percent in 1996, he said.
According to the Statistics Directorate, an estimated 13 percent of Morocco's 27 million inhabitants live below the line of poverty and earn around $300 per year.
Morocco's GDP reached 316 billion dirhams ($34.7 billion) in 1966 or an average $1,300 per head.
Morocco's illteracy is one of the highest in the Arab World with an estimated 55 percent of total population, including more than 70 percent of the women, officials said.

The bank is expected to grant Morocco an average $300 million per year during the three-year plan, to be devoted mainly to basic education, health, social and vital infrastructure projects, the report said.
The Moroccan government is expected to examine the World Bank strategy plan this week while holding constructive talks with its official delegation in Rabat, a official source said.
